note: The session map's kernel classes (workflow/session_map.py, read only there). A launch's class is, in order: the output head when its matmul computes the vocabulary's rows (the header's lm_head); an engine row below whose pattern matches its name (the engine's rows, then those of the engines it lists in kernel_families.json `also`); a matmul by its op (data/kernel_families.json shapes rows, or an installed manifest's entry) and the format family of the tensors a decode's join ties it to (a prefill has no join: its dense matmuls are one class, `unsplit`; a decode matmul tied to none is `unjoined`); else its family (data/kernel_families.json) through `families`. A class names what the search would have to express, not a model's role: rows are keyed by kernel class and phase. `unattributed` lists the classes whose time the map cannot put a floor under (no family, or a matmul tied to no tensor): their share of the step is the map's own coverage check. Words for every class are in data/plain_words.json session_map.classes.

rows.why: the sparse attention's selection: the radix top-k over the indexer's scores, the mask it builds and its compaction to indices (ggml-cuda top-k, flash_attn_mask_to_sparse_indices; mods 01/03/05 and decode-topk-fused)
the sparse attention's indexer, scoring the pooled keys (lightning_indexer_kernel_*)
the KV cache write of a forward's new tokens and their position encoding (rope_*, k_set_rows*: SET_ROWS into the cache)

prefill_phase.why: llama-server runs the draft head in its own llama_context, so its prefill catch-up runs on its own CUDA stream; the target's prefill is the stream with the most launches in the window (prefill-gap-20261117 pf_ana: target stream 15, draft 17, on the 2026-11-17 traces)
